articles.summary: Founded in 2019, the National Equity Trade Certification and Network is building long-term pathways for equity and legacy cannabis businesses to thrive. Based in Oakland and operating nationwide, the network connects purpose-driven brands with the resources, relationships, and infrastructure needed to succeed—centering community, culture, and economic repair at every step.
articles.title: Inside the National Equity Trade Certification and Network

articles.summary: February 2026 brought significant cannabis policy updates in both California and New York, with implications for licensed dispensaries, distributors, beverage manufacturers, and multi-state operators. California’s proposed AB 1826 would refine recall, embargo, and product destruction procedures, directly affecting compliance workflows and inventory risk management. In New York, lawmakers enacted a zoning fix protecting more than 150 licensed dispensaries from closure, while a newly introduced bill (A10191) proposes allowing liquor and wine stores to sell low-potency (≤5mg THC) cannabis beverages under a new retail permit structure. Together, these developments signal continued regulatory evolution in mature and emerging cannabis markets, reinforcing the importance of legislative monitoring for operators navigating compliance, retail expansion, and beverage distribution strategy in 2026.
articles.title: February 2026 California and New York and Cannabis Policy Updates

articles.summary: At a Gotham and Cultivated Media event in New York City, Will Brophy, COO of Nabis, took the Hot Seat for a rapid-fire conversation on the realities shaping today’s cannabis industry. From federal rescheduling and banking reform to capital constraints and market maturity, Brophy cut through common misconceptions to offer a grounded, operator-first perspective on what’s actually changing and what challenges remain.
articles.title: In the Hot Seat: Will Brophy on Rescheduling, Banking Reform, and the Reality of Cannabis Markets
